name: Emden
title: Thickness Measurement in Emden | Car Carriers, Ems and Dockings
description: Ship thickness measurement in Emden for car carriers, ro-ro, bulk and offshore vessels: deck and hull UTM, pre-docking gauging and repairs behind the sea lock.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging in Emden for Vehicle Carriers, Ro-Ro Ships and Ship Repair
intro: Emden is Germany's westernmost North Sea port, at the mouth of the Ems by the Dutch border, and it is best known for the vehicle carriers that load cars from the Volkswagen plant beside the harbour. Behind its sea lock lies a sheltered harbour with a repair and conversion yard, quays for wind turbine components, bulk and breakbulk, and the island ferries leave from the outer harbour. Gauging requests here range from car decks to full docking programmes, and each is carried out by technicians who travel from India for that job.

highlights.h: Vehicle carriers at the car terminals
highlights.p: Emden is one of Europe's leading car ports, with vehicle carriers calling to load German-built cars for export. In the gap between discharge and loading the car decks are briefly clear, and deck plating, ramps and hoistable-deck supports can be measured and crack-tested.

Emder Werft und Dock, a repair and conversion yard with more than a century of history in the port, takes ships that can pass the sea lock. A docking there gives the full window for renewal survey gauging and support to the surveyor during the close-up survey.

Onshore wind towers, nacelles and blades are imported over Emden's quays, and the shipyard has added ship recycling to its repair work. Both bring ships that need condition data: heavy-lift vessels for their decks, and ageing ships whose owners must choose between another survey cycle and a final sale.

port.h: Emden, the Ems estuary and the sea lock
p: Emden lies on the north bank of the Ems estuary where the river opens into the Dollart, looking across the water to the Netherlands. Ships approach from the North Sea along the Ems fairway past Borkum, a long passage through shifting sands that is kept open by dredging and navigated with pilots. The port has two parts: an outer harbour open to the tide, and an inner harbour behind the sea lock, where the water level is held and ships lie sheltered from the weather. That shelter is one reason German authorities have designated Emden as an emergency port for ships in difficulty. Niedersachsen Ports owns the port infrastructure, and the Volkswagen factory, the town's dominant employer, sits right beside the harbour basins.

Cars dominate the port's identity. Vehicle carriers call regularly to load new Volkswagen Group cars and other vehicles for export and to discharge imports, which makes Emden one of the largest car-handling ports in Europe. Around that trade sit others: onshore wind components imported for German wind farms, cable drums for grid projects, forest products, bulk and general cargo, and service traffic for offshore wind farm operation and maintenance. The ferries and fast craft to Borkum sail from the outer harbour. Upstream on the Ems, the Meyer Werft yard at Papenburg builds cruise ships that pass down the river on their delivery voyage, an event that occupies the estuary for a day or so whenever it happens. Smaller coasters and the dredgers that keep the fairway open complete the local fleet.

Inspection demand follows the same split. Vehicle carriers need deck and ramp work fitted into short calls, and because they rarely see a dry dock outside their survey dates, owners use terminal calls to follow the condition of car decks that have taken years of rolling loads. The shipyard offers the opposite case: a ship inside the sea lock for weeks, with staging, lighting and gas-free spaces available for a complete programme. The inner harbour is non-tidal and protected, so weather seldom interrupts work there, although winter storms on the Ems can delay a ship's arrival at the lock. For heavy-lift ships at the wind quays, the stay is set by the pace of unit-by-unit discharge, and a long tower or blade shipment can keep a ship in port for several days.

facilities.h: Yard, terminals and quays for gauging in Emden
p: Emder Werft und Dock is the port's repair and conversion yard. It works behind the sea lock on ships that fit through it, and it has recently gained the permits to recycle ships as well. For a vessel docked at the yard or lying at its quays, gauging follows the thickness measurement plan and the attending surveyor's close-up list, using the yard's staging and services, and plates found below the renewal limit are marked so the steel crew can start without waiting for the report. The yard also fabricates for industry and wind energy, so steelwork capacity is at hand when renewal turns out to be extensive.

Outside the yard, gauging is done afloat. At the car terminals the window is the gap between discharge and loading, when decks are clear and the crew can lower hoistable decks and open ramps. Breakbulk and wind component quays give longer stays, especially when heavy-lift ships land towers and blades one unit at a time. Ships waiting in the inner harbour between employments offer the longest windows, because the protected, non-tidal water makes them easy to reach and safe to work on in most weather.
list: Emder Werft und Dock — in-dock and alongside gauging for renewal and docking surveys, with steel renewal marked for the yard.
Car terminals in the inner harbour — car-deck, ramp and hoistable-deck gauging on vehicle carriers between discharge and loading.
Wind component and breakbulk quays — tween-deck, tank-top and hatch cover readings on heavy-lift and multipurpose ships.
Bulk and forest product berths — hold and tank-top measurement after discharge.
Outer harbour berths — short jobs on island ferries and offshore service craft between trips.
Waiting berths behind the sea lock — longer condition, pre-purchase and pre-sale surveys on idle ships.

context.h: Port state control, ship recycling and EU rules in Emden
p: Emden falls under the Paris MoU, with port state control carried out by BG Verkehr's Ship Safety Division. Vehicle carriers have drawn closer attention since fires aboard several of them in recent years, and inspectors and owners alike now look harder at fire protection, ventilation and the condition of car decks and their supports. Thin deck plating under years of wheel loads and condensation is not the most visible defect on a PCTC, but it becomes one of the most consequential when a ship is asked to carry heavier electric vehicles on the same decks.

Ship recycling has given Emden a new link to EU rules. Under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, every ship calling at an EU port must carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, and EU-flagged ships may only be recycled at facilities on the European List of ship recycling facilities. With the Emden yard now licensed by German authorities to recycle ships, owners weighing a final sale against another survey cycle have a German option to consider, and gauging gives them the steel figures behind either decision. EU ETS, in force for shipping since 2024, and FuelEU Maritime, since 2025, add emissions obligations that weigh most on older tonnage.

jobs.h: Gauging jobs that come up in Emden
jobs.p: Emden jobs split between quick terminal work on vehicle carriers and full programmes at the yard. For car carriers the scope is usually a defined set of decks, ramps and supports, finished between discharge and loading. For dockings the team works to the yard's schedule beside the class surveyor, and for ships facing recycling or sale the request is often a condition baseline. Heavy-lift ships at the wind quays add tween-deck and crane structure. Each scope is agreed with the superintendent and, where a docking is involved, with the yard's project manager before the team leaves India, and readings are passed on daily. Typical jobs:
list: A PCTC between discharge and loading: lower-deck and fixed car-deck plating, ramp structure and hoistable-deck brackets, with magnetic particle testing at the brackets.
A ro-ro ship docked at Emder Werft und Dock for its renewal survey: full thickness measurement programme, close-up survey support and steel renewal marking.
A heavy-lift ship discharging wind turbine towers: tween-deck pontoons, tank top and crane pedestal structure gauged during the unit-by-unit discharge.
An offshore service vessel alongside in the inner harbour: deck, ballast tank and piping readings ahead of a new charter.
An older ship lying in the inner harbour before a sale decision: owner's condition gauging of holds, tanks and decks to compare further trading with recycling.

logistics: Bremen Airport is the usual arrival point, with Hamburg and Amsterdam Schiphol as alternatives for long-haul flights; Emden is linked to Bremen by rail and motorway. The ship's agent arranges ISPS access to the car terminals and quays, while the yard issues its own passes and induction for dockings. Technicians coming from India travel on Schengen visas, so dates for a docking should be sent as soon as the slot is fixed, and terminal calls as soon as the vessel's rotation is known.

faqs.q: Can a car carrier be gauged during a single Emden call?
faqs.a: A defined part of it can. With clear decks between discharge and loading, a team can usually measure a set of car decks, ramps and hoistable-deck supports, plus selected ballast tanks if the crew prepares them in advance. For a complete programme on a large PCTC, owners often spread the work over two or three calls, since the same ships come back to Emden on regular rotations.

faqs.q: Does the sea lock limit which ships can use the Emden yard?
faqs.a: Yes. Everything that docks or lies alongside at the yard has to pass the sea lock, so length, beam and draught set the limit, and the yard or the agent confirms whether a given vessel fits before a docking is booked. Ships too large for the lock dock elsewhere in north-west Europe, and our team can travel to whichever yard the owner chooses.

faqs.q: Is gauging useful for a ship that may be recycled?
faqs.a: It often is. Before choosing between another survey cycle, a sale for further trading and recycling, an owner needs to know how much steel the ship would require to keep going. A condition gauging of holds or decks, ballast tanks and the bottom gives that figure, and the visit can be coordinated with the surveyor who is updating the ship's Inventory of Hazardous Materials.

faqs.q: Can island ferries and offshore craft be gauged between trips?
faqs.a: Yes, within the time they lie alongside. Ferries and fast craft on island services keep tight timetables, so work is usually done overnight or on a planned lay day and focuses on specific tanks, deck areas or piping. Offshore service vessels waiting in the harbour between jobs give more time, and their crews can prepare tanks and voids without cargo pressure.

faqs.q: How does the weather on the Ems affect a job?
faqs.a: Mostly through the approach. Winter storms and poor visibility can delay a ship's arrival at the sea lock, so we follow the agent's updated estimate before fixing travel. Once a ship is inside the lock, the harbour is sheltered and non-tidal, and gauging on board continues in almost any weather, which makes Emden a dependable place for longer programmes.
